guide.summary: Customers authorize the app with per-user OAuth 2.0 and the app obtains a user token. The App Folder content-access option limits actions to the app folder, and the list-folder endpoints require files.metadata.read.
guide.recommendation: Customers authorize the app with per-user OAuth 2.0 and the app obtains a user token. The App Folder content-access option limits actions to the app folder, and the list-folder endpoints require files.metadata.read.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth 2.0 authorization is documented for user-scoped apps
findings.detail: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 so each user signs in and grants the app access; the returned access token is passed as a Bearer token. The code flow is the recommended flow for all app types.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects their own individual account.

evidence.quote: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0
Overview When working with the Dropbox APIs, your app will access Dropbox on behalf of your users. You’ll need to have each user of your app sign into dropbox.com to
be used by your app in subsequent API calls for that user. It should be passed with the Authorization HTTP header value of Bearer <oauth2-access-token>

findings.title: Register the app and configure redirect URIs before testing
findings.detail: Register the app in the Developer Console to obtain an app key and secret and register exact redirect URIs. Customers connect to the single registered app and do not register their own.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you’ll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console
You’ll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console
Do not instruct your users to register their own Dropbox application to use your app - you just need to register your app once. Your end-users will connect to that

findings.title: files.metadata.read scope for listing folder entries
findings.detail: The list_folder and list_folder/continue endpoints require files.metadata.read, which covers reading metadata for files and folders in the app folder. Continuation uses the cursor until has_more is false; no content download or write scope is selected.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing names through list_folder and continuation pages.

findings.title: App Folder content access limits actions to /apps folder
findings.detail: The App Folder option lets the app act within its scopes only on data within its app folder. This is the access boundary the customer request requires.
findings.appliesWhen: App is created with App Folder content access.

evidence.quote: App Folder: Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder only (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable for

steps.title: Create a scoped Dropbox app with App Folder access and files.metadata.read
steps.detail: In the Dropbox Developer Console, create a scoped app with App Folder access, enable files.metadata.read on the Permissions tab, and save. Record the app key and secret. Do not enable content read/write or sharing scopes.
steps.doneWhen: App exists with App Folder access, only files.metadata.read enabled, and app key and secret recorded.

evidence.quote: Choose Scoped access as the API type.
App folder : Access limited to a single folder in the user’s Dropbox.
Scope Description files.metadata.read View information about files and folders

fields: App key and secret from the Settings tab

steps.title: Register exact redirect URI and choose the code flow with a client secret
steps.detail: Add the exact redirect URI in the OAuth 2 section of the Settings tab. Use the authorization code flow with the client secret for a server-side app. Construct the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code, and include token_access_type=offline only if background access is needed. This request needs no background access, so omit it.
steps.doneWhen: Redirect URI is registered exactly and the authorization URL uses client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code.

evidence.quote: is the recommended OAuth flow for all types of applications. In order to implement it, your application should:
Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user
for your application. Add them under Redirect URIs in the OAuth 2 section of the Settings tab. Dropbox checks that the specified redirect_uri parameter in your Authorization URL matches one

steps.title: Complete consent as a test customer and verify the callback carries a code
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser signed into a test Dropbox account, approve the app, and confirm the redirect returns a code in the query string. This step does not exchange the code. Send the state parameter if your app uses one.
steps.doneWhen: Browser redirects to REDIRECT_URI with a code query parameter.

evidence.quote: Construct a Dropbox authorization URL , with your application’s client_id and redirect_uri (if applicable) and specifying the response_type of code , and present it to the user
After the user has approved your app, they’ll be sent back to your app with an authorization code
The redirect_uri is optional with the code flow - if unspecified, the authorization code is displayed on dropbox.com for the user to copy and paste to your app.

fields: Test Dropbox account used for consent

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the code at the token endpoint using the app key and secret with grant_type=authorization_code, the code and the redirect_uri. This is an unexecuted authorization step until run with a real code; store the returned access_token securely.
steps.doneWhen: Token endpoint returns an access_token and expires_in in JSON.

evidence.quote: Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls
Your application exchanges the authorization code for an access token that can be used to make secure calls to the Dropbox API (not shown)
In your request to the /oauth2/token endpoint, pass the code_verifier with your generated value instead of the client_id .

fields: AUTH_CODE from the callback query string
APP_KEY and APP_SECRET from app settings

steps.title: List the first page of the app folder

steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 with entries array, cursor and has_more boolean. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.detail: While has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the cursor from the previous response, collecting entries[].name each time. Stop only when has_more is false. Do not invent a cursor.
steps.doneWhen: Final page returns has_more=false and all entries are collected across pages. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
